subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - latency/throughput SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the FintechCorp infra team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a validation run on Redwood Dedicated.

Summary of FintechCorp SLOs (from call):
- Latency targets (streaming use case): p50 < 60 ms, p95 < 180 ms for end-to-end per-token streaming latency (chunked streaming to client).
- Throughput: steady-state 12 req/s average, burst up to 60 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: target 45 concurrent active streams with a typical prompt length ~350 tokens, response average ~220 tokens.
- Availability: want 99.9% availability SLA for dedicated pool during peak hours.

Questions / clarifications we need from your side to size the run finely:
1) Model family & quantization: which model do you want validated (e.g., Llama 2 70B, Mistral-7B, custom fine-tuned 13B)? If you want to test multiple variants, please prioritize.
2) Max context window in production (tokens).
3) Percentage of requests expecting streaming vs. non-streaming (approx).
4) Any special decoding constraints (e.g., beam search, nucleus sampling top_p) that materially affect per-token cost.

Initial capacity guidance (internal rough estimates — final numbers after we run workload tests):
- H100 (4x H100 80GB reserved): estimated ~1200-1600 tokens/sec aggregate for our baseline 13B-ish model at 8k context with streaming, supports ~40-60 concurrent streams depending on chunking and batchability.
- A100 (4x A100 80GB): ~700-1000 tokens/sec aggregate, higher variance under streaming, better for larger context models but increases reserved cost.
- L4 (8x L4): cost-effective for smaller models and high-concurrency lightweight streams (~200-350 tokens/sec aggregate).

Recommended next steps:
- You provide the sample prompts (we can use the anonymized file you mentioned).
- Redwood will run a 48-hour dedicated validation with a mirror traffic generator (we'll simulate your burst patterns and streaming chunk sizes).
- We'll produce a performance report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput curves, GPU utilization, and recommended pool sizing (GPU type + count + reserved throughput).
- Meeting: schedule a 30-min results review + sizing recommendation with FintechCorp + Redwood engs.

Attachments: I attached a short validation plan and a template for the Fintech workload profile (fintech_capacity_profile.xlsx), plus sample prompt list (fintech_sample_prompts.txt).

Next actions: please reply with answers to the 4 clarifying questions and confirm a preferred week for the validation run (we have capacity starting Nov 8).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0119

---
Attachment: fintech_capacity_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_perf_plan_v1.pdf (PDF stub)
Attachment: fintech_sample_prompts.txt (text file)

From: Anna Patel <anna@fintechcorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael O'Leary <michael.oleary@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Aditya — that recap looks right. Answers inline below plus a few extra details.

1) Model: we'll start with a fine-tuned 13B (decoder-only) model; plan to evaluate a 70B only if the 13B misses quality. We plan to test quantized FP16 and int8.
2) Max context: 4096 tokens for the validation run.
3) Streaming vs non-streaming: ~85% of production requests will use streaming (progressive updates).
4) Decoding: sampling with top_p=0.95, temperature=0.8. No beam search.

Traffic profile: steady 12 req/s during business hours, typical burst to 60 req/s for 15-30s during settlement windows. Concurrency target is 45 active streams (concurrent clients).

Budget & timeline: We'd like a sizing recommendation and an order-of-magnitude cost estimate for a monthly Dedicated pool. Can Redwood provide a ballpark for: 4x H100 reserved vs 6x A100 reserved vs 8x L4 reserved? We'll evaluate TCO vs latency tradeoffs.

We're good for a validation run the week of Nov 8. Please confirm the exact slot and what you'll need from our infra team (VPN, ingress IPs, sample traffic generator).

Thanks,
Anna Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCorp
anna@fintechcorp.com
(612) 555-0890

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@fintechcorp.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-call recap and next steps

Anna — great, thanks for the details. A few follow-ups from the SE side so we can make the validation run as close to production as possible:

- For streaming behavior, can you confirm your preferred chunk size (in tokens) and average inter-chunk interval (ms)? This materially affects KV-cache behavior and network overhead.
- For the sample traffic generator, we can accept either a replay of recorded requests (preferred) or we can run a synthetic generator if you provide distributions (prompt length, response length, inter-arrival times).
- Can your infra team open egress to the Redwood validation cluster and provide temporary SSH access for our validation engineer? If not, we can run the traffic generator from your side and have Redwood collect telemetry via Prometheus endpoints.

Preliminary sizing notes (for the 13B quantized int8 streaming workload you described):
- 4x H100: expected to comfortably meet p50 ~35-45ms, p95 ~120-160ms across your 45-concurrency streaming profile. Headroom for bursts to 60 req/s.
- 6x A100: p50 ~55-75ms, p95 ~160-220ms; good if you prefer the A100 economics and larger context headroom.
- 8x L4: likely fail the p95 target for this model/streaming profile — better suited to smaller models or non-streaming high-concurrency patterns.

I'll draft the exact validation scenarios (steady-state, 3 burst patterns, token-length variations) and include the Prometheus + perf counters we'll capture. If this sounds good I'll attach the run plan and proposed slot (Nov 9 09:00 - Nov 11 09:00 PST, 48-hour run).

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - latency/throughput SLO follow-up (confirmed slot & prep)

Anna — confirmed. We've reserved the Nov 9 09:00 PST slot for the validation run (Marissa will own the test harness and telemetry). Next steps / what we need from FintechCorp by end of day Nov 8: 

1) Provide the anonymized sample prompts file (attached template already, but please confirm final file).
2) Confirm chunk size for streaming (we typically test 64-token and 128-token chunks; tell us which you use in prod).
3) Provide a short VPN/IP allowlist window or confirm you'll run the traffic generator from your environment (if so, we'll send the Prometheus scrape config).

Deliverables after the run (by Nov 13):
- Full performance report (p50/p95/p99 latencies, per-gpu token/sec, batch sizes seen),
- Recommended Dedicated pool sizing (GPU type & count) and expected monthly cost ranges for each option (4x H100, 6x A100, 8x L4),
- Observability exports (prometheus metrics dump, example traces),
- Action items / recommended config changes (batching, prefix caching, quantization guidance).

I've attached the validation run plan (redwood_dedicated_perf_plan_v1.pdf) and the updated fintech_capacity_profile.xlsx. If all good, we'll send calendar invites to your infra and engineering leads and loop in our provisioning team for the reserved pool.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated.

Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
